reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the MedicationRequest StructureDefinition report, the two direct SearchParameter findings whose `affectedResources` include MedicationRequest, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings as background only. The deterministic aggregate was compared after forming the resource-level conclusion.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 MedicationRequest was FMM 3/trial-use, so it does not carry a normative compatibility burden, but it is mature enough that common prescribing, dispensing, safety, workflow, and generated-API breaks need clear justification and low-cost preservation should be preferred.

overall.oneLineConclusion: MedicationRequest keeps its identity, but R6 remodels enough central prescribing content that a structured migration program is unavoidable while low-cost compatibility preservation still matters.

reasoning.thesisMd: MedicationRequest is not removed or replaced, but it is not a mostly stable resource with a few edge-case breaks. The required medication field changes wire/model shape, dosage instructions move from repeating `Dosage` to a single `DosageDetails`, reason and reported-source data are remodeled into new structures, safety/protocol linkage fields are removed, and reference/terminology/search behavior also shifts. Real R4 instances and generated clients will need coordinated transformation rather than just validator updates.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The core migration shape is a same-resource major model remodel. The common and safety-critical axes are `medication[x]` to `CodeableReference`, `dosageInstruction` 0..* `Dosage` to 0..1 `DosageDetails`, and the R4 `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` and `reported[x]` patterns moving to R6 `CodeableReference` or split fields. Additional hard breaks remove or rename optional but clinically meaningful fields such as `detectedIssue`, `instantiatesCanonical`/`instantiatesUri`, and `dispenseRequest.performer`, and target-aware validators can reject legacy `basedOn` and `performer` references.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because migration is already unavoidable, preserving every old wire name is not equally valuable. However, the resource identity is stable and several breaks appear cheap to avoid or at least cheap to provide transition behavior for: retaining legacy reference targets, keeping a deprecated same-type nested alias, preserving optional traceability/safety links, and avoiding canonical SearchParameter reuse. Those are still worth standards attention because they reduce avoidable churn without blocking the larger R6 model.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The highest-cost compatibility alternatives are for the central normalized models: keeping both R4 medication choice properties and R6 `CodeableReference`, or keeping both repeating R4 dosage instructions and single R6 `DosageDetails`, would create duplicate safety-critical representations and conflict rules. By contrast, preserving `ImmunizationRecommendation` on `basedOn`, preserving `Device` on `performer`, aliasing `dispenseRequest.performer` to `dispenseRequest.dispenser`, retaining deprecated `instantiates*` and `detectedIssue` links, and not repurposing the `medications-date` canonical URL are comparatively low-cost or high-safety-value measures.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior impact is concentrated in SearchParameters. The `medications-date` canonical URL is especially standards-review-worthy because it moves from MedicationRequest to MedicationAdministration while keeping the same canonical, which can silently bind generated clients or metadata-driven query builders to a different resource and clinical meaning. The broad reference-target/chaining finding also affects MedicationRequest, but it mostly follows structural target-list modernization and is a migration chore unless a still-valid old target was dropped. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation and special-search findings are real platform context but are not counted as MedicationRequest-specific conclusions.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: After independent review, I agree with the deterministic aggregate's high-level result: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable=Yes`, `migrationShape=major-model-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The reason is not the count alone; it is the combination of common required-field remodeling, clinically sensitive dosage redesign, multiple local hard breaks, and a direct SearchParameter canonical repurpose. I also agree with its caution that individual Revisit findings remain important despite the resource-level migration burden.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Structural conclusions are high confidence from the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions. Remaining uncertainty is mainly about official cross-version maps, final R6 ballot changes, live terminology expansions, and whether HL7 has intended replacement guidance for removed traceability and safety links.

findingConsiderations.title: medication[x] became medication CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This required, common, safety-critical field changes R4 choice-property wire names into an R6 `CodeableReference` object. The change is probably justified by the R6 modeling direction, but it guarantees parser, serializer, mapper, and generated-model work for essentially all mature MedicationRequest implementations.

findingConsiderations.title: dosageInstruction changed from repeating Dosage to single DosageDetails
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the clearest clinically sensitive migration driver: common R4 arrays of `Dosage` become a single `DosageDetails` structure, with potential loss or expert mapping around alternatives, sequences, timing, and rendered text. It remains standards-review-worthy even though the resource already needs migration.

findingConsiderations.title: reported[x] was split into isRecordOfRequest and informationSource
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The split is a coherent cleanup of a mixed R4 choice, but it invalidates old `reportedBoolean` and `reportedReference` property names. It is part of the local mapping program rather than a reason by itself to reject the R6 redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: reasonCode and reasonReference merged into reason CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R6's `reason` CodeableReference follows the same modernization pattern as medication and is common clinical content. The change is disruptive but mostly a structured mapping chore once CodeableReference migration is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: basedOn target changed from ImmunizationRecommendation to RequestOrchestration
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Dropping `ImmunizationRecommendation` while adding `RequestOrchestration` is a target-aware validation break. Keeping both targets would not create duplicate fields or hard precedence rules, so this is a low-cost compatibility preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: performer repeats and replaces Device target with DeviceDefinition
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The widening and repetition are compatible, but removing the R4 `Device` target makes specific-device performers invalid in target-profile-aware validation. Allowing both `Device` and `DeviceDefinition` during transition would preserve old instances while still enabling the R6 distinction.

findingConsiderations.title: dispenseRequest.performer renamed to dispenseRequest.dispenser
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a same-type nested rename from `performer` to `dispenser`. The new name is clearer, but a deprecated alias or retained old path with clarified wording would be a low-cost way to avoid breaking strict parsers, FHIRPath, indexes, and generated accessors.

findingConsiderations.title: instantiatesCanonical and instantiatesUri removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These optional links preserve traceability to protocols, guidelines, and order sets. Their removal is a hard instance break with modest apparent preservation cost, so the standard should either retain deprecated elements or provide an explicit replacement mapping.

findingConsiderations.title: detectedIssue references removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Removing the direct link can lose or obscure safety context for interactions, duplicate therapy, and dosage alerts when a MedicationRequest is migrated without its related DetectedIssue graph. Even if `DetectedIssue.implicated` is the preferred R6 direction, this optional safety-relevant link deserves transition support or clear replacement guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: status required binding adds ended and changes hierarchy
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 status codes appear retained, so this is not an R4-to-R6 instance break. It does matter for bidirectional gateways because R6 `ended` has no exact R4 status and needs mapping policy.

findingConsiderations.title: courseOfTherapyType binding strengthened to extensible
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element shape and value set URL are stable, and extensible binding creates terminology QA pressure rather than a structural break. It does not materially affect the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: intent comment now says intent is expected to be immutable
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new immutability guidance can change server workflow behavior for systems that updated proposal/plan/order intent in place. It is a meaningful lifecycle migration concern, but it is semantic guidance rather than an instance-shape driver.

findingConsiderations.title: `medications-date` keeps its canonical URL but moves from MedicationRequest to MedicationAdministration
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important direct behavior finding. Reusing the same canonical URL for a different base resource and clinical meaning can silently misdirect metadata-driven clients; using a new canonical for the MedicationAdministration search or deprecating the old MedicationRequest search is a low-cost, high-value compatibility fix.

findingConsiderations.title: Reference SearchParameters changed target lists, affecting chaining, type modifiers, and reverse include expectations
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: MedicationRequest is among the affected resources, and target-list changes can break typed modifiers, chaining, and generated enums. For this resource, the issue largely tracks the underlying reference-target changes, so it is migration work plus follow-up where a still-valid old target was dropped.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This and the other shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings can affect MedicationRequest-serving systems, but they are not MedicationRequest-specific because the assessed resource is neither Resource nor DomainResource. They should be handled in the platform/base-resource review, not used to inflate this resource conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search metadata issue is relevant operating context for all resource servers, but it is not a local MedicationRequest model change and therefore does not drive this review's resource-level migration classification.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Give `dosageInstruction` dedicated standards review and migration guidance, including how to preserve multiple R4 dosage lines, alternatives, sequence/timing semantics, and rendered text when converting to one R6 `DosageDetails`.

Do not repurpose the `medications-date` SearchParameter canonical URL across resource bases; use a new canonical for the MedicationAdministration date search or retain/deprecate the MedicationRequest canonical without changing its base meaning.

Preserve low-cost legacy compatibility where feasible: keep legacy `basedOn` and `performer` reference targets during transition, alias `dispenseRequest.performer`, and either retain or explicitly replace `instantiates*` and `detectedIssue` links.

Publish authoritative R4-to-R6 maps for MedicationRequest covering CodeableReference conversions, reported/source splitting, status `ended`, performer/course role terminology, and down-conversion behavior for R6-only optional fields.

caveats: The R6 input is ballot4, so final publication could alter some findings.
No live terminology expansions or official ConceptMaps were used in this resource-level review.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed only as context and not scored as MedicationRequest-specific breaks.
Official HL7 rendered diffs or cross-version maps could refine replacement guidance for removed traceability and safety fields.
